chapterName: Late Republic: Antony, Octavian and the End of the Republic (44-27 BCE)

questions.question: Why did Cleopatra decide to kill herself in 30 BC?
options: Her last army deserted to Rome
She learned she would be paraded in his triumph
questions.explanation: Cleopatra tried to bargain but learned she was destined to be paraded in Octavian's victory procession. She died on 12 August 30 BC.
questions.sourceQuote: Cleopatra tried to bargain, but learned she was destined to be paraded in Octavian's victory procession (*triumphus*).

questions.question: Where did Antony and Octavian renew the lapsed triumvirate in 37 BC?
questions.explanation: At Tarentum in southern Italy they renewed it for five more years, and Antony lent ships for the Sicilian war in exchange for promised troops.
questions.sourceQuote: In 37 BC Antony and Octavian met at Tarentum in southern Italy and renewed the triumvirate, which had quietly lapsed, for five more years.

questions.question: Which provinces did Antony grab for himself with an illegal law in June 44 BC?
questions.explanation: Antony gave himself the provinces of Gaul, roughly modern France and northern Italy, from where he could menace Rome itself.
questions.sourceQuote: In June he pushed through an illegal law giving himself the provinces of Gaul, roughly modern France and northern Italy.

questions.question: After seizing the consulship in August 43 BC, what did Octavian do? (select all that apply)
options: Confirmed his adoption as Caesar's son
Cancelled Antony's status as a public enemy
Pardoned the assassins and recalled them
Set up courts to condemn the assassins
questions.explanation: Octavian confirmed his adoption, had the assassins condemned in their absence, and quietly cleared Antony, paving the way for their deal.
questions.sourceQuote: He confirmed his adoption as Caesar's son, set up courts to condemn the assassins in their absence, and quietly cancelled Antony's status as a public enemy.

questions.question: When was the label "Second Triumvirate" first used?
questions.explanation: The term is modern, first used in the 17th century, and many historians now avoid it as misleading. The three called themselves the board of three for restoring the republic.
questions.sourceQuote: We call this the Second Triumvirate, but that label is modern, first used in the 17th century, and many historians now avoid it as misleading.

questions.question: Off which place in Sicily did Octavian's admiral win the decisive sea battle of 36 BC?
questions.explanation: Octavian's closest friend and admiral won the decisive battle off Naulochus on 3 September 36 BC.
questions.sourceQuote: His closest friend and admiral won the decisive sea battle off Naulochus, in Sicily, on 3 September 36 BC.

questions.question: Which of these was part of the uneasy compromise reached right after Caesar's murder?
options: Antony was named dictator for a year
The office of dictator was abolished
The assassins were exiled from Italy
questions.explanation: The compromise pardoned the assassins, confirmed Caesar's decisions and abolished the office of dictator. It did not last long.
questions.sourceQuote: The assassins were pardoned, Caesar's decisions were confirmed, and the office of dictator was abolished.

questions.question: Which prominent victim of the proscriptions was killed along with his brother, nephew and son?
options: The admiral who ruled the seas from Sicily
The general who had commanded in Spain
The orator who had attacked Antony in speeches
The tribune who passed the lex Titia
questions.explanation: The orator who had attacked Antony in blistering speeches was killed with his brother, nephew and son. The same man had earlier persuaded the Senate to back Octavian.
questions.sourceQuote: The orator who had attacked Antony in a series of blistering speeches was killed, along with his brother, nephew and son.

questions.question: How did Octavian treat Perusia after it fell?
options: He massacred its councillors and burned it down
He handed it intact to his veterans
He sold all its citizens into slavery
He pardoned everyone and left it unharmed
He spared the town but executed Antony's brother
questions.explanation: Octavian let Antony's family go and spared their soldiers, but massacred the town's councillors and burned Perusia to the ground.
questions.sourceQuote: When the town fell, he let Antony's family go and spared their soldiers, but massacred the town's councillors and burned it to the ground.

questions.question: How did Antony help Cleopatra secure her throne?
options: By marrying her in a Roman ceremony
By bribing the Senate to recognise her
By exiling her rival to Cyprus
questions.explanation: Antony had Cleopatra's sister killed to secure her throne. He later gave Cleopatra territory to build a fleet.
questions.sourceQuote: They soon began an affair, and Antony helped her secure her throne by having her sister killed.
